says: Both built-in microphones of surya work on mainline (2026-11-17): the bottom one (AMIC1) on the WCD9375's ADC1, the top one (AMIC3) on ADC2 at INP3 with its own master port 3, over the TX SoundWire bus (capture DAI 1), the TX macro's decimators and the DSP's TX_CODEC_DMA_TX_3; the sound server records them through UCM's Mic and TopMic. The phone proves it every boot: mic-hears-speaker and mic-top-hears-speaker find a soft 1 kHz beep 40-60 dB above the noise. Kernel: linux-phone-oco/linux test/surya-mic, four WCD9375 fixes (PRs 3-6). Decision 2026-11-17-microphones-analog-wcd-path, resting on microphones-are-analog. Dead ends, not to retry: DMICs and the VA macro's path - surya has no digital mics (the DMIC routes were Qualcomm's QRD board) and this ADSP refuses the VA port (bolero-v1-capture-family); start-up ringing then exact zeros means no input reaches the decimator - look at the SoundWire stream, not the DMA (mic-zeros-meant-no-input); the codec's sleep pin state pulled it off the bus (microphone-codec-drops-off). Test kernels are built from pushed branches (2026-11-17-test-kernels-from-branches). Open: upstream through sm7150-mainline PR 60 (mic-upstream); the headset mic not yet tried (verify-headphone-mic-earpiece). Pixel 2 and 2 XL: not known yet.

lpoco-health is linux-phone-oco's one health suite, shipped on the phone (renamed from devlab-health, same checks and results). Shell checks print pass|fail|skip lines; a static Rust runner gathers them into the test_results shape. What the phone finds out itself (no SIM, no modem, no network) is a detected condition reported as a skip; what somebody chooses is a switch (lpoco-health off TEST --reason ..., on, list) kept on the phone with who and when. Docs hold only hardware facts and results. Provisioned by devlab suite put now (lab-built runner; migrates old reports) until the Alpine package can be signed. Carried by research 2026-11-17-lpoco-health-landscape, decision 2026-11-17-lpoco-health, backlog lpoco-health (on the phone queue), lab-tools #75.

Nothing runs on walleye yet; the phone is in fastboot, unlocked, A/B, bootloader mw8998-003.0085.00, nothing written (walleye-fastboot-first, google-walleye-bootloader-first-look). Mainline v7.3 has no Google board; kcxt's walleye dts is a 13-line stub; porthole's mainline-7.2.2 kernel (263 patches) is a working Pixel 2 XL port whose walleye board file nobody has run (walleye-mainline-prior-art). Walleye's parts (S6E3FA5 command-mode panel, Synaptics touch, WCD934x + TAS2557, DRV2624, PMI8998 charger/gauge) are in google-walleye-vendor-kernel-hardware; what mainline already has and lacks is walleye-mainline-reuse. First boot: v0 boot.img, dtb appended with qcom,msm-id 0x124/0x20001, no bootargs in the dts, USB 2.0 gadget as the only sign of life (walleye-first-boot-recipe); unknown: walleye's boot.img header, whether fastboot boot works with a mainline dtb and the dtbo. Decision 2026-11-17-walleye-first-kernel: v7.3 + a minimal own dts; eight items with proofs in the walleye backlog (walleye-kernel-dts first).

says: Surya does not reach the SoC floor: after real 15 s s2idle cycles (cluster state 0x4100c244 taken, CX/MX votes 0, sleep set clean but SH0 x=1,y=3) cxsd, aosd and ddr read 0; wake and way back are solved (decisions 2026-11-17-way-back, serial-wakeup-off). Ruled out by measurement: cluster parameters and a stopped audio DSP / all DSPs - but those were stops of DSPs that had run, so latched votes are not excluded. Others reach the floor on mainline s2idle only by removing holders (research 2026-11-17-floor-research); the path is decision 2026-11-17-floor-research-path: read what is held (cmdline, clocks, icc), boot with DSPs never started, then subtract WLAN, USB, the SH0 owner, one per cycle, each judged by way-back.sh cycle 15 bt-on and the soc-sleeps check, which fails until the floor. Not known yet: the holder; whether this firmware fills the counters (adsp 0, apss/display/gpu empty); standby current (sleep-standby-current).

says: One roof: the command is lpoco, a git-style dispatcher (argenv) that runs the family's programs lpoco-bringup, lpoco-health, lpoco-lab (today's devlab, kept as another name), lpoco-tone; one pin (device.toml [tools] lpoco), one release, one MCP door (lpoco mcp). lpoco-bringup makes a device's first boot images: it wraps mkbootimg and avbtool and crates for cpio, compression and dtb, and owns the checks, the swap of one part against a control image and the reproducible initramfs. Devices follow by pin and extend beside it (data in [boot], hooks, a rust-script on the pinned library): no rebase; changes go back as pull requests recorded as upstream items; updates by pin bump. The phone keeps its small static lpoco-health. Rhizoid's missing parts are on its own backlog (git-rhizoid.github.io PR 28). Decision 2026-11-17-bringup-in-lab-tools; research bringup-tools-landscape, bringup-home-follow-and-rhizoid, bringup-family-names, bringup-one-roof. Not built: lpoco-dispatcher with bringup-image-v0 first (failing tests lpoco-runs-subcommand-by-path, pack_v0), then rename of lab and tone, pin-and-hooks, release, mcp door.

Phone-side pieces (what lpoco puts on a phone) are decided, not built. Every lab phone's pieces ride the lab-tools package - the keep-awake first, as lpoco-health awake (lpoco-awake) - and walleye's gadget init and ACM console go under lpoco bringup (bringup-generic-init); a device names roof pieces by token and keeps only its own files (decision 2026-11-18-phone-side-pieces-under-the-roof). Drift is named, not trusted: the phone reports each package version and each declared file's git blob id every boot (health-reports-pieces), and lpoco host check names a stale one from the last gathered report (phone-pieces-drift-named, its failing test written first; text in research/phone-side-pieces/2026-11-18/). device.toml stays data, declared once in Rust with a schema projected per release (decision 2026-11-18-device-manifest-schema-from-rust, manifest-one-schema and one row per device repository). Upstream: three questions (sxmo autosuspend backoff, sxmo suspend stops by profile, qcom_wdt armed in suspend) wait on the author's word. Hand-over: phone-side-pieces-how-it-stands.

Our forks live under the author's account - grenudi/sxmo-utils (fork-sxmo-utils, a mirror of sr.ht) and grenudi/linux (fork-linux), transferred from the organisation so one history stays (decision 2026-11-18-upstream-forks, research upstream-forks-landscape). Each upstream item is a topic branch off the untouched tracking branch; a never-rebased lab/test branch is what phones run - sxmo-utils as a tagged lab apk (sxmo-utils-lab-apk), kernels by each lab's route. One upstreams lane coordinates (upstreams-lane, waiting on orchestration). Written, unsent, each waiting on its phone proof then the author's word: the sxmo series of three (sxmo-autosuspend-backoff, sxmo-suspend-stop-by-profile, sxmo-surya-sensors-suspend; research sxmo-suspend-fixes; spec in the series) and the RFC kernel series pmic-wdt-wake-in-suspend, which supersedes qcom-wdt-armed-in-suspend (research pmic-wdt-way-back; proofs surya-pmic-wdt-proof, walleye-pmic-wdt-proof in the device bases). rhizoid is not used yet; what it needs went to it as rhizoid-carries-mail-forks.

The repository graph (idealkb, docs, device-template, the device bases, lab-tools' pins, the forks) was measured on 2026-11-18 (research base-graph-measured): 12 edges, 3 moved by a job, 6 by hand, 5 behind; nothing carries a change up - own is a one-way exit, an edited followed file stops at a person - and the parts contract is declared by the template and read by docs. The world (base-graph-world) offers no Rust or shell tool for root-level files both ways (copybara only, JVM) and four rules: one owner per file, named overrides with a status, pins per ancestor, a scheduled integrator report. Decided 2026-11-18-device-layer-from-docs: idealkb -> docs -> every device base, docs giving the device layer from device-layer/, the template a follower keeping its seed files; own needs an item; edits go up as PRs; graph-drift.sh daily; forks tracked daily; git-rhizoid after, by conformance. Nothing built yet: graph-drift.sh 36 FAIL; next idealkb's from-prefix (upstream item), then device-layer-in-docs (backlog base-graph). How it stands: base-graph-how-it-stands.

device-template (made 2026-11-17 as a GitHub template from what surya proved; a lab holds data, tools are lpoco's) has two children, surya-lab (re-based by hand) and google-walleye-lab (Use this template). Its 10 statements and 4 device tables reach them only by hand; the pin is a date (research device-template-drift-measured, template-drift.sh). Decision 2026-11-18-device-template-follows-by-release (the template releases and is followed) is superseded by 2026-11-18-device-layer-from-docs: the device layer comes from docs (device-layer-in-docs), so a contract such as parts or steps has one home beside the feed that reads it; the template becomes a device base like the others, pinning idealkb and docs and keeping its made-once seed files (template-classifies-its-files, template-follows-docs); the labs follow docs (surya-follows-template, walleye-follows-template); template-releases and template-followed-by-update-pins are closed, not done. The manifest's shape is the schema's (template-manifest-schema). The whole graph: summary base-graph.

Bring-up steps are data: docs keeps the generic steps (bringup_stages, bringup_steps, bringup_step_edges; goal steps linux-runs, daily-usable-phone, complete-phone), each device base claims its own status per step (steps table and record step in docs' device layer, released in 0.18.0; data/steps.json, steps = 1 in its devicebase.toml), and docs pulls the claims into step_status (feed-device-steps; unclaimed, invalid or unreadable reads unknown, not known yet, with why). Read with tad q bringup-chain [--device] [--goal STEP] and tad q milestone-steps (milestones name step:ID@DEVICE, a goal derived from its needs; surya-daily-phone). Kept whole by make verify: test-steps-contract, test-feed-device-steps, check-bringup-steps, test-bringup-chain-goal, test-milestone-steps. Decisions 2026-11-18-bringup-steps-generic-in-docs-status-in-each-base and ...-phone-stages-and-goal-steps; research bringup-steps-landscape, -coverage-map, -phone-stages; tad q prior-art. No base has claimed yet: bringup-chain-walleye.sh and daily-phone.sh fail for want of claims (every step unknown). Waiting: the lanes' claims (walleye-steps-claimed, surya-steps-claimed, each needs steps = 1), the guidebook, helper map and runner.

Nura (postmarketOS until 2026-09-27) is the distribution surya runs whole - the v26.06 image, the generic qcom-sm7150 port, its sm7150-mainline kernel package, the UI packages - and lpoco lab kernel boots by its names (pmos.conf, the postmarketOS title). walleye runs no Nura yet. We redistribute nothing of Nura's; we redistribute sxmo-utils (AGPL-3.0-only) on our apk page, whose source directions are missing. Nura forbids AI-made contributions, so agents send or prepare nothing for it; giving back directly is the author's own act. Recorded in landscape nura and upstream nura-pmaports (research nura-relation-how-it-stands, decision 2026-11-19-nura-relation). Open: apk-pages-origin-licence, built-on-nura-line, surya-base-image-named, lpoco-nura-names-one-place, nura-give-back-by-hand (waits on the author).

Which distribution our phones build on. Recommended, waiting on the author's word (decision 2026-11-19-base-distro): stay on Nura - it alone carries surya's SM7150 (community port by the sm7150-mainline people, kernel 7.1) - and carry a thin device layer of our own in the apk repository the conveyor publishes; walleye, which no base carries, starts on the same base with its own kernel and device packages. Arch-based, Fedora, openSUSE and NixOS bases carry neither SoC, so the layer would become our own phone OS; Mobian's SM7150 is staging-only and unpublished, so it is the fallback, measured off the phone first. Ubuntu Touch and Droidian (Halium) are out on the author's word. Giving back: kernel open on any base; Nura only by the author's hand; Alpine open while council #697 is; sxmo closed by SourceHut.
